findings.issue: The SPEC-08 and SPEC-10 acceptance tests take 5.4 s and 6.8 s locally without coverage (about 2x in CI sweeps). Both workloads are what the spec asks for: 300 Tough hands run twice (recorded and unwrapped), and 2,000 Tough plus 2,000 Mixed hands. They sit in the sweeps group, not the unit group, and stay well under the 120 s timeout. Acceptable.
findings.evidence: vitest verbose: earlier showdowns 5409ms, compose 1332ms, postflop cap 6838ms. Unit group: 47 files in 3.1 s, slowest test 1.7 s (existing cli.test.ts), and every new unit test is 58 ms or less.
findings.fix: None required. To trim CI time, the Mixed half of SPEC-10 (it only asserts more than 0 postflop bets) could use 500 hands, if the spec owner agrees.

findings.issue: `expect(Object.keys(seamKeys)).toHaveLength(3)` always passes at runtime. The real guard that PlaytestSeams has no new key is the `Record<keyof PlaytestSeams, true>` annotation, and only typecheck enforces it.
findings.evidence: seamKeys is a literal with 3 keys, so the runtime assertion cannot fail. A new required key fails `npm run typecheck`, which SPEC-12 runs.
findings.fix: Optional: add a short comment saying typecheck is what enforces it, or leave it as is.

summary: Every SPEC item is implemented and its tests would catch a broken implementation. Line-up shard planning: 27 shards in preset-major order, seeds 1000000 + 100(p+1) + size, and leftover hands go to the earliest shards (unit tests at 28 hands and 1e9, acceptance test at 1,000,000). The combined report's per-line-up/size lines are checked for both a passing run and a failed shard (0 in its cell). The default million run is unchanged: the --hands 900 hash 1b561d…176a, the 10k/size 6 hash aacd5e…8e01 and the tough-2000 hash 757901…4cbd all match, re-run locally. The workflow is dispatch-only with contents: read and the same checkout/setup-node SHAs as million.yml and ci.yml, has no schedule, and runs one 30-minute job. Earlier showdowns: the last 1000 are kept, the list resets on a violation or abandoned hand and on a new sit-and-go, and each hand gets a new array, so lists already handed out never change. The unit test snapshot catches mutation, and the acceptance test's stored references would catch a shared mutable array. Bot decisions are unchanged: the summary equals the unwrapped run and the baselines match. composeChecks returns every hook's violations joined in hook order; it does not stop at the first one. playHand still stops the hand at the first action that has any violation, and the test checks chips ids come before style-check. The AC#6 test counts postflop bet/raise per street from final.actions with MAX_BETS_PER_STREET = 4 and requires at least 1 capped postflop street plus 0 violations (spec measured 908 bets and 7 capped streets). No unit-group test exceeds 5 s. The style-bots acceptance tests take 1.3–6.8 s, which is acceptable. Only NITs.
